business.headline: Food inflation at 7.74%: Which items are burning a bigger hole in your pocket?The festive season is meant to bring cheer, but rising grocery bills could leave families with less to spend on celebrations. From kitchen essentials to everyday vegetables, here's what is making household budgets tighter.

South Korea's Kospi tumbles over 6% as CXMT concerns hit chip stocksThe Kospi was down 382.18 points, or 5.93%, at 6,002.06 as of 0213 GMT. A fifth consecutive session of losses would mark the index's longest losing streak since September 2024.

HCLTech jumps 6%, TCS surges over 5%: Why are IT stocks rising today?HCLTech's strong September-quarter results triggered a rally in IT stocks led by TCS, Infosys and Tech Mahindra. The move has shifted attention to whether AI-led demand and deal momentum can support a broader sector recovery.

Sensex jumps over 600 points: 4 factors driving stock market rallyThe Sensex rose more than 600 points on Tuesday as IT shares led a broader market advance. The rally highlighted how domestic buying is cushioning foreign outflows despite inflation, crude and bond yield concerns.

Sensex jumps over 300 points as market rebounds; IT stocks among top gainersBenchmark indices opened higher on Tuesday, with the Sensex and Nifty recovering in early trade. The rebound came as investors weighed crude oil, global cues and geopolitical uncertainty.

India's growth gets an IMF boost, but an oil shock could spoil the partyThe IMF has raised the growth bar for India, but whether the economy can clear it will depend on how long the oil shock lasts and how much damage it does along the way.

Adani Group begins construction of 10 towers with 10,432 homes for Dharavi residentsPranav Adani performed the bhoomi poojan for the Matunga rehabilitation project, launching construction of 10,432 homes for eligible Dharavi residents. The project sets out phased handovers, new amenities and long-term building maintenance under the Dharavi redevelopment plan.

Who Are Robert E Hall and Michael Woodford, Nobel Economics Winners 2026?The two economists were recognised for developing new macroeconomic models that have improved the way policymakers understand economic changes and decide when to act.

Retail inflation rises to 5.54% in September from 4.83% in August as food prices climbRetail inflation stood at 6.08% in rural areas in September, compared with 4.88% in urban areas. This indicates that price pressures were higher in rural India than in cities.

Sensex falls 548 points despite record SIP inflows. 4 reasons whyThe Sensex fell 547.65 points, or 0.76%, on Monday, while the Nifty 50 declined 157.10 points, or 0.70%, to close at 22,363.35. ITC and Tech Mahindra were among the top losers.

Robert E Hall and Michael Woodford awarded 2026 Nobel Prize in EconomicsThe award recognises their work on economic principles that help explain how economies respond to changes and how policymakers can work towards greater stability.

Foreign investors flee, Dalal Street pays the priceForeign investors have pulled over Rs 3 lakh crore out of domestic equities this year. High US bond yields, expensive crude and a weakening rupee have made matters worse, leaving domestic investors to absorb the blow.

SIPs hit record high, equity mutual fund inflows jump 31% in September: AMFINet inflows into equity mutual funds rose 31% from August to Rs 38,307 crore in September, the highest in five months, according to data released by the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) on Monday.

Inter-state migrant workers: A long road from legal protection to implementationIndia's migrant labour laws have evolved, but gaps in implementation, reduced safeguards and weak monitoring continue to leave workers vulnerable to exploitation.

IMF says AI boom is keeping global growth at 3%, Asia set to gainInternational Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said on Monday that strong investment in AI infrastructure was keeping global growth at around 3%, despite the pressure from an energy supply shock.

60% of borrowers have EMIs eating up family income. Is festive debt worth it?Festive discounts can make spending more tempting, while easy credit makes it easier to buy things without paying upfront. But when does convenient borrowing become a debt trap?
Another bloodbath brewing? Sensex sinks 500 points as 4 factors rattle D-StreetAt 11.30 am, the Sensex stood at 71,941.36, while the Nifty was down 132.15 points, or 0.59%, at 22,388.30.

EPFO clarifies EPS eligibility after Rs 25,000 wage limit hike: Who qualifies?The Ministry of Labour and Employment has increased the monthly wage ceiling for mandatory EPFO coverage from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000, effective September 17, 2026.

Therapy costs nearly Rs 2,000 a session. Can your health insurance help?Mental health treatment is legally entitled to insurance parity, but therapy claims often fail in practice. The gap usually lies in policy terms that cover hospitalisation or limited app counselling, not regular outpatient sessions.

TVS succession plan sees Venu Srinivasan and Mallika differ over asset ownershipThe main point of disagreement is whether assigning businesses to the next generation also settles the ownership of family wealth.

entertainment.headline: Gondhal review: Secrets, patriarchy and a ritual that cannot hide the truthRelease Date:Fri Oct 09, 2026 Gondhal movie review: Santosh Davakhar's Marathi film uses a traditional ritual to tell a story of desire, power and revenge. With strong performances and an unusual setting, it makes for an intriguing watch, even if the writing does not always keep pace with its ambition.

Drishyam 3 writer explains how Jaideep Ahlawat's cop isn't exactly the villain In an interview, Drishyam 3 writer Aamil Keeyan Khan said Jaideep Ahlawat's SP Rajveer Singh Tomar should be seen as an antagonist rather than a villain.

Imran Khan should be deported: BJP's Kirit Somaiya seeks action after Mumbai protest BJP leader Kirit Somaiya demanded actor Imran Khan's deportation after he joined the Mumbai protest. The row has put Khan's citizenship status and the detention of protesters under fresh focus.

Rajinikanth says he identifies as a bus conductor, loved the job more than acting At the Jailer 2 Super Show, Superstar Rajinikanth said he still sees himself as a bus conductor despite decades of fame. The remarks, along with his tribute to fans and mentor K Balachander, underscored the humility and discipline he says guide him.

Rs 25 per show to being Garba queen: The incredible story of Falguni Pathak Singer Falguni Pathak's rise from a child performer in Mumbai to a Navratri mainstay was built through live shows, Gujarati folk music and Indipop hits. Her decades-long bond with audiences has made her a constant presence at Garba and dandiya celebrations.

Heartbroken Bryan Cranston and Breaking Bad co-stars mourn RJ Mitte in moving posts Bryan Cranston, Aaron Paul and Dean Norris have mourned Breaking Bad co-star RJ Mitte. Cranston, who played his father in the series, revealed they'd been texting about meeting for lunch just weeks before his death at 34.

A little SRK-Kajol magic: Nushrratt Bharuccha finds joy after spinal surgery Nushrratt Bharuccha shared a hospital video as Shah Rukh Khan and Kajol played on television during her recovery. The post marked a hopeful update after spinal surgery following her Bali accident.

Rashmika, Vijay Deverakonda begin Ranabaali release week with Tirupati visit. Watch Rashmika Mandanna and Vijay Deverakonda visited the Lord Venkateswara Temple in Tirupati before Ranabaali's release. The visit, after their Chennai meeting with Vijay, has drawn fan attention around their third film together.

Vijay Deverakonda needs a comeback. Can Ranabaali save his sinking stardom? Vijay Deverakonda's Ranabaali could be the comeback he needs after a string of box-office disappointments. Can the Rashmika Mandanna-starrer revive his career and change public perception?

Actor Selma Blair pleads not guilty to in-flight assault charges, out on $20k bail Selma Blair was charged with second-degree assault after an alleged disturbance on a Delta flight from Los Angeles to New York. Her team said she had suffered a medical emergency. After her release on bail, the case was transferred to Queens Criminal Court.

Jailer 2 advance booking: Rajinikanth's sequel sees strong demand with Rs 34 crore Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 has opened advance bookings strongly ahead of its 15 October release. Early demand is being led by Chennai, while ticket prices vary sharply across major centres.

Shane Gillis' misogynistic SNL monologue and Dan Levy's response explained American comedian-actor Shane Gillis drew backlash after his Saturday Night Live monologue included misogynistic remarks and an on-air expletive. Actor Dan Levy slammed Gilllis for his remarks and stressed that public objectification fosters harmful environments for women.

Drishyam 3 box office Day 11: Ajay Devgn's biggest hit nears Rs 500 crore globally Ajay Devgn's Drishyam 3: The Conclusion is nearing the Rs 500 crore mark worldwide, showcasing a strong box office performance in its 11th day. The thriller has become Devgn's highest grosser, crossing significant milestones both in India and overseas.

Jailer 2: The challenge of following Rajinikanth's Rs 600 crore blockbuster Rajinikanth said Jailer 2 grew from unresolved threads in the first film's ending. Now, Nelson Dilipkumar must turn that setup into a fresh conflict, not just a bigger repeat. Will he?

RJ Mitte dies at 34; US media reports suicide as cause RJ Mitte, who played Walter White Jr in Breaking Bad, died on Monday at 34 in Brownsville, Texas. Remembered as an actor and disability rights advocate, he used his platform to push inclusion on and off screen.

US actor Selma Blair in custody after mid-air chaos on flight leaves 2 injured Selma Blair was taken into custody after an alleged mid-air incident on a Delta flight to New York. The episode left two crew members injured and is now under FBI investigation.

Kritika Kamra returns to 'hellhole' X after Instagram censors 'truthful voices' Actor Kritika Kamra said she returned to X after Instagram restricted her posts during the ongoing protests demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. She backed people speaking up for citizens' rights while warning off trolls.

Mohanlal praises Ajay Devgn's Drishyam The Conclusion, calls it befitting end Actor Mohanlal has praised actor Ajay Devegan's thriller, Drishyam: The Conclusion and congratulated its team. In his video message he mentioned that he was truly impressed by the film's climax.

Already a favourite: Vijay Deverakonda-Rashmika Mandanna after meeting CM Vijay Actors Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna met Tamil Nadu Chief Minister-actor Vijay. The meeting comes ahead of the release of the duo's next film, Ranabaali.

general news.headline: Out of sight, out of mind? Jantar Mantar goes off protest map, Oppn cries foulThe CJP and the opposition have cried foul after the Delhi Police de-notified Jantar Mantar as a designated venue for protests. It has led to allegations that the move was aimed at making it harder for citizens to take their protests to the seat of power.

Keralam Congress raises stink over poll process that brought it to powerThe Congress-led UDF swept to power in Keralam months after the SIR of voter rolls. MP Shashi Tharoor had suggested that might have helped the party win the Assembly elections. Now, the Congress-led government has passed a resolution seeking the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar and questioning the SIR. This has handed the BJP ammunition to slam the Congress over the very electoral process that brought it to power.

No appraisal at Zoho, but Vembu doubles down on 'NRIs return from US' stanceTech entrepreneur Sridhar Vembu has renewed his appeal to Indians and Indian-origin engineers and entrepreneurs to return to India from the US. Vembu had just earlier today said there would be no appraisal at Zoho, a software company founded by him, this year even as he was trying to stave off mass layoffs.

You terrorist: Muhammad Yunus faces anger of Bangladesh expats in New YorkMuhammad Yunus, the head of the earlier interim government in Bangladesh, was confronted by angry Bangladeshi expatriates at New York's JFK Airport. The heckling showcases the anger over his tenure after the fall of the Sheikh Hasina regime. Yunus is travelling abroad amid calls for probes against him and his Grameen Group.

Has Rahul Gandhi used Neha Bora to pull the rug from under CJP's feet?AISA leader Neha Bora, one of the most visible faces of the CJP July protest, stood alongside Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra during the Congress-led march to the Supreme Court. Is Rahul using Bora to draw the youth-led protest movement into his own political orbit, potentially leaving the CJP fighting for the spotlight?

SC pauses criminal defamation trial against Rahul Gandhi over remark against PMThe Supreme Court has put the brakes on the criminal defamation trial against Rahul Gandhi over his 2018 jibes at Prime Minister Narendra Modi during the Rafale deal controversy. The case, filed by a BJP worker, centres on Gandhi's alleged "Commander-in-Thief" and "Choro Ke Sardar" remarks.

Musk ranted about India's 'oligarchs', Bernie Sanders now turns the charge on himElon Musk accused Indian oligarchs of blocking Starlink's India entry. The outburst has sharpened scrutiny of his own vast political spending in the United States.

Video: CJP's Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka jump gate to sneak into Jantar Mantar, detainedThe CJP leaders' group entered the area from the side of the Janata Dal (United) office premises near Jantar Mantar. Police subsequently detained those who had entered the site. Delhi Police may also register an FIR in connection with the incident.

Flood of farmers and Babri: Why protest site moved from Boat Club to Jantar MantarA flood of farmers led by Mahendra Singh Tikait in 1988 and the security concerns following the Babri Masjid demolition in 1992 pushed the Congress government to restrict mass protests at New Delhi's iconic Boat Club lawns. In 1993, Jantar Mantar emerged as the capital's new square for dissent. Nearly 33 years later, the BJP-led Centre has redrawn Delhi's protest map.

Live: Rahul to host high tea for INDIA bloc leaders today, joint presser likelyAnti-ECI Protest Live: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi has invited INDIA bloc leaders, civil society members and student organisations for high tea at his residence at 4 pm, with a joint press conference also likely to take place. Sources have said that the Opposition's future course of action might be announced at the presser. Meanwhile, CJP's Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained after jumping a gate to enter Jantar Mantar. In a post on X, Das declared, "Jantar Mantar has been reclaimed." The high tea meeting comes a day after the Opposition's march to the Supreme Court over SIR exercise. Delhi Police has registered an FIR in connection with the march, while the deployment of 20,000 paramilitary personnel in the national capital has been extended by four weeks amid continuing protests, Ministry of Home Affairs sources said. Follow indiatoday.in for the latest updates.

Shubman Gill, Shafali Verma clean sweep ICC awards for September 2026Shubman Gill has equalled the record for most ICC Player of the Month awards after his big scores against the West Indies. Women's team opener Shafali Verma earned the September honour after starring in India's Asia Cup and Asian Games triumphs.

From kitchen essentials to everyday vegetables, here's what is making household budgets tighter.

Sidhu Moose Wala's brother recreates signature thaapi gesture at Toronto concertSidhu Moose Wala's younger brother, Shubhdeep Singh Sidhu, attended the late singer's hologram show in Toronto, where he recreated his signature thaapi gesture. He was joined by their parents, Balkaur Singh and Charan Kaur.

Punjab anti-drug activist Parvinder Jhota shot dead by medical store owner on cameraIn the video, Jhota is seen accusing the pharmacy owner of selling drugs to the man and threatening to take legal action against him. An argument soon breaks out, escalating into a fatal shooting.

Lucknow tycoon falls to death from girlfriend's flat; cops recover sex toys, drugsThe victim, Shiv Sharma, was wearing only his underwear when he was found, while police recovered sex toys and sexual enhancement medicines from the apartment. His mother, Ranjana Sharma, has accused his girlfriend, social media influencer Shraddha Dubey, of harassing and blackmailing him, and alleged that she pushed him to his death.

Imran Khan should be deported: BJP's Kirit Somaiya seeks action after Mumbai protestBJP leader Kirit Somaiya demanded actor Imran Khan's deportation after he joined the Mumbai protest. The row has put Khan's citizenship status and the detention of protesters under fresh focus.

Why airlines fear power banks: The science behind lithium battery firesAn IndiGo Delhi-Chennai flight was diverted to Hyderabad after smoke was detected from a passenger's personal electronic device. The incident has renewed focus on how failing lithium-ion batteries can become a fire hazard in flight.

Ayodhya battle peaks: Yogi dares Akhilesh, SP chief says confirm your ticket firstUP CM Yogi Adityanath has challenged Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav to contest against him from Ayodhya in the 2027 Assembly polls. Reacting to it, Akhilesh expressed doubt that Adityanath could secure a ticket for himself. The exchange has brought Ayodhya back to the heart of UP's political narrative, two years after the BJP lost the Faizabad seat in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls.

Sex-for-marks row: Sacked by JNU, Congress MP claims witch hunt by 'khap panchayat'Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam has rejected sexual harassment allegations after his dismissal from JNU. He called the action a witch hunt after the university enquiry found the accusations substantiated.

Heartbroken Bryan Cranston and Breaking Bad co-stars mourn RJ Mitte in moving postsBryan Cranston, Aaron Paul and Dean Norris have mourned Breaking Bad co-star RJ Mitte. Cranston, who played his father in the series, revealed they'd been texting about meeting for lunch just weeks before his death at 34.

Sridhar Vembu cancels Zoho appraisals, says working hard to avoid mass layoffsZoho founder Sridhar Vembu has confessed that the homegrown company is facing a difficult time. Vembu says that Zoho has cancelled appraisals this year, and is trying hard to avoid layoffs amid rising expenses due to AI.

Madurai influencer asks for sweets, gets TVs, fridges on COD; begs to end prankA Madurai-based Instagram creator said pranksters flooded his home with unwanted COD orders after he shared his address seeking Diwali sweets. The escalating deliveries forced him to leave town.

Luck Maxxing: Why techies are quitting jobs to create their own opportunitiesA growing number of technology professionals are rethinking traditional career paths and taking risks to create their own opportunities. The trend, known as 'luck maxxing', focuses on increasing the chances of success by meeting new people, experimenting with ideas and stepping outside familiar routines.

No tolls: 60 countries back declaration opposing fees on shipping through straitsOver 60 countries have backed an EU declaration opposing fees on ships using international straits amid disruption in the Strait of Hormuz. The move signals collective resistance to restrictions on lawful navigation as Iran links access to its demands.

sports.headline: Shubman Gill, Shafali Verma clean sweep ICC awards for September 2026 Shubman Gill has equalled the record for most ICC Player of the Month awards after his big scores against the West Indies. Women's team opener Shafali Verma earned the September honour after starring in India's Asia Cup and Asian Games triumphs.

Ronaldo's Al-Nassr match delayed by an hour after missile threat in Saudi Arabia Cristiano Ronaldo scored as Al-Nassr beat Uzbekistan's Neftchi Fergana 3-1 in their AFC Champions League Elite fixture in Riyadh on Monday. The match was delayed by an hour after Saudi Arabia's Civil Defence issued a safety warning amid missile threats in the region.

Murali Sreeshankar flown to London for urgent surgery, government to cover cost Murali Sreeshankar is set to undergo ligament reconstruction surgery on his right ankle. Union Minister Suresh Gopi confirmed that the central government will bear the entire cost of the procedure and fund the athlete's rehabilitation.

CSK CEO hopeful of MS Dhoni's return despite missing entirety of IPL 2026 Chennai Super Kings CEO Kasi Viswanathan is hopeful that MS Dhoni will return for IPL 2027 despite missing the entire 2026 season due to injury concerns. At 45, Dhoni is yet to publicly reveal whether he believes his body can withstand the demands of top-level cricket for another season.

R Sridhar warns India's fielding woes could worsen in chilly New Zealand R Sridhar has warned that India's fielding woes could worsen on their New Zealand tour. He stressed the need to build a clear fielding culture as India continue to struggle with dropped catches despite their success in major tournaments.

Cricketer Prithvi Shaw, Akriti Agarwal reconcile weeks after calling off engagement Prithvi Shaw and Akriti Agarwal have rekindled their relationship weeks after calling off their engagement, with the actor and influencer admitting that outside opinions influenced her decision and urging people to respect their fresh start.

When Sunil Gavaskar, the bowler, dreamt of dismissing Gary Sobers Sunil Gavaskar recalled how he once dreamt of dismissing West Indies legends Rohan Kanhai and Garfield Sobers in consecutive deliveries when he fancied himself as a bowler. He also shared childhood memories of watching Sobers bat in India and reflected on the all-rounder's extraordinary legacy.

Likho, it's your job: Shami sends message to fitness critics through reporters Mohammed Shami claimed four wickets for Bengal against Delhi in the Ranji Trophy season opener before delivering a pointed message to fitness critics, insisting he remains focused on bowling, playing cricket and enjoying his game.

Renshaw hurts South Africa with bat and ball as Australia near Durban Test win SA vs AUS, 1st Test Day 4: Matt Renshaw starred with scores of 190 and 82 before claiming his maiden Test wicket to put Australia on the brink of victory against South Africa in Durban. Chasing 421, the hosts ended Day 4 at 102 for 4, needing a major rearguard effort to save the Test.

At 38, Umesh Yadav takes five for new team Punjab after two-year Ranji Trophy gap Umesh Yadav returned to first-class cricket with a five-wicket haul for Punjab against Assam in the Ranji Trophy. The spell signalled a strong start to his new stint after his move from Vidarbha.

Meet Adam Gilchrist of Pakistan: How an Aussie legend inspired a teenager's name Pakistan's teenager Adam Gilchrist grabbed attention after scoring 117 for Kamran Public School, with his name tracing back to his father's admiration for Australian legend Adam Gilchrist.

Stephen Fleming brings Chennai Super Kings flavour to England's Test coaching setupStephen Fleming has added a Chennai Super Kings flavour to England's Test coaching setup by bringing in former colleagues James Foster and Eric Simons ahead of the South Africa tour.

Injury blow for India as Rishabh Pant ruled out of New Zealand tour with A teamRishabh Pant has been ruled out of the first two India A matches in New Zealand with a side strain, with Kumar Kushagra named as his replacement. The injury raises questions over Pant's availability for the senior team's upcoming Test series.

England drop Zak Crawley, reward 8 players with central contracts for 2026-27England have dropped Zak Crawley and Luke Wood from their central contracts for 2026-27, while expanding the contracted group from 30 to 39 players, including eight new full-contract recipients.

Abishek Porel hits Ranji century days after bail in rape case, breaks down in tearsAbishek Porel scored an unbeaten century for Bengal against Delhi and broke down in tears in Kalayani on Monday. The knock came weeks after he was granted bail in a case involving allegations of rape and criminal intimidation.

Alexander Zverev dethrones Sinner, becomes first German men's World No. 1 since BeckerAlexander Zverev has become the first German men's World No.1 since Boris Becker in 1991, following Carlos Alcaraz's third-round exit at the Shanghai Masters. Jannik Sinner's absence since Wimbledon due to a knee injury had boosted Zverev's chances of finishing the season at the top of the ATP rankings.

4 days after Asian Para Games send-off, India yet to release official squadFour days after the Sports Ministry's send-off ceremony for India's Asian Para Games contingent, the official squad list is yet to be released. The send-off ceremony was itself marred by protests from para-shooters who accused officials of corruption.

WPL history-maker returns. USA pacer joins Mumbai Indians for 2027 editionUnited States fast bowler Tara Norris has joined Mumbai Indians for the WPL 2027 season after being traded from UP Warriorz at her existing fee of Rs 10 lakh.

India vs Sri Lanka 1st ODI to stay in Delhi, BCCI rejects venue change reportsBCCI secretary Devajit Saikia has dismissed reports of a venue change, confirming that India's first ODI against Sri Lanka will remain in Delhi on December 13. The two teams are scheduled to play three ODIs and three T20Is during Sri Lanka's December tour of India.

Suspended from Portugal team, Cristiano Ronaldo claims he is the best in historyCristiano Ronaldo has declared himself the best player in football history. In an interview with CNN Portugal, he insisted that his goalscoring record and current form are not receiving the recognition they deserve.

Dravid by name, dynamite by nature: Anvay in six-hitting spree in Vinoo Mankad Trophy17-year-old Anvay Dravid smashed 85 off 41 balls as Karnataka posted 418 for four against Delhi Under-19 in the Vinoo Mankad Trophy on Monday. The innings extended his strong run after a century against Chandigarh last week.

Ravindra Jadeja slams Ranji Trophy century, builds towards New Zealand TestsRavindra Jadeja scored his 16th first-class century, making 102 for Saurashtra against Chhattisgarh in the Ranji Trophy. The knock comes ahead of India's two-Test tour of New Zealand, giving the all-rounder valuable time in the middle before the international assignment.

Abhishek Verma eyes LA Olympics, 2030 Commonwealth Games after Asian Games snubAbhishek Verma is determined to fight his way back into India's national team after missing the historic Asian Games campaign that secured the country's first Olympic quota in compound archery. The 37-year-old is targeting the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and the 2030 Commonwealth Games at home, while backing India to win multiple archery medals in LA.

PV Sindhu, Lakshya Sen handed tough draws in Denmark OpenPV Sindhu and Lakshya Sen face challenging opening-round tests at the Denmark Open. Sindhu is set to take on world No. 1 An Se-young while Lakshya has been drawn against third seed Chou Tien Chen.

Abhishek Sharma saw West Indies' plan coming. Here's how he respondedAbhishek Sharma smashed a 30-ball 69 to help India beat West Indies by 14 runs in the third T20I and take a 2-1 lead in the five-match series. The opener explained how he countered West Indies' plans to contain him, while stressing the need to stay ruthless against a side capable of fighting back.

India vs West Indies: The vanished fearIndia's white-ball series against the West Indies brings back memories of a team that once inspired fear across the cricketing world. Through his father's recollections of the old guard, Pranav Jain traces the rise and fall of a cricketing giant.

Churchill Brothers raced against time to prepare for ISL, then beat Mumbai CityChurchill Brothers had just 25 days of training before their maiden Indian Super League campaign, with late arrivals and visa delays adding to the challenge. They began with a 2-1 win over two-time champions Mumbai City FC at Fatorda.

After 19 seasons, Maharashtra's Ankit Bawne is still alive and chasing India dreamRanji Trophy 2026-27: After a disastrous Ranji Trophy season left him questioning himself, Ankit Bawne returned with a century against Services. At 33, after nearly two decades in domestic cricket, the Maharashtra batter is still chasing his India dream.

Abhishek Sharma's power comes with a plan, Dinesh Karthik explains whyIND vs WI: Abhishek Sharma's explosive 69 off 30 balls against West Indies in Indore underlined his growing dominance in T20 cricket. Dinesh Karthik has now highlighted the opener's improved game awareness and credited mentor Yuvraj Singh for helping him evolve.

Naman Dhir and the making of India's next three-dimensional cricketerIND vs WI: Naman Dhir since making his debut has been more impressing with the ball than many anticipated, making him a genuine prospect for being India's next big spin all-rounder in white-ball cricket.

NCERT deletes Azad Pak, adds China's aggression reference in Class 12 textbookThe NCERT has made final changes to its Class 12 Political Science textbook syllabus for the upcoming academic year, including a revision in reference to India's border situation with China, Azad Pakistan, Article 370 and more.

NEET row: Bihar cops find 6 post-dated cheques 'issued for question paper brokers'Six post-dated cheques which were suspected to have been issued in favour of mafia demanding over Rs 30 lakh from each candidate seeking alleged leaked question paper ahead of NEET held last month were recovered by Bihar Police.

Forest fires surge tenfold from 2004 to 2017: Causes, impact and preventionAmidst a relentless surge, intense forest fires are now multiplying tenfold, casting a menacing shadow over our flora and fauna. Year by year, their fiery grip tightens, threatening ecosystems far and wide, now extending their reach to impact human lives.

Fresh plea in Supreme Court to recall NEET results, reconduct examsA fresh petition has been filed in the Supreme Court to recall the National Entrance cum Eligibility Test - Under Graduate (NEET-UG) 2024 results and re-conduct fresh examination after discrepancies in the declared results.

NTA issues clarification after NEET result controversy over toppers, high cut-offIn a detailed statement, the National Testing Agency (NTA) said that the increase in cut-off and number of toppers in the NEET-UG reflect the competitive nature of the exam and maintained that the test's integrity has not been compromised.

Exclusive: Arvind Kejriwal claims 'BJP succession war, PM backing Amit Shah'Speaking exclusively to India Today TV, Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal claimed that there is a "succession war" within the BJP. He also claimed that the ruling party is "not fighting the Lok Sabha elections as a team".

4 medical students arrested in Bihar for appearing as proxies for NEET aspirantsFour MBBS students who appeared in place of NEET aspirants in the medical entrance exam were detained in Bihar's Purnea.

NEET-UG question paper not leaked, claims baseless: National Testing AgencyThe reports claiming question paper leak in the medical entrance exam NEET-UG are "completely baseless and without any ground", the National Testing Agency (NTA) has clarified.

Left sweeps JNU students' polls, Dhananjay is first Dalit presidentThe Left swept the Jawaharlal Nehru University Students' Union (JNUSU) polls, winning all four posts and trouncing the RSS-affiliated ABVP. JNU students' body election on March 22 after 4 yearsThe Jawaharlal Nehru University Students' Union (JNUSU) polls will take place on March 22, more than four years after the last elections were held in September 2019.

UP 12th board exam math, biology papers leaked on WhatsApp, complaint filedThe mathematics and biology question papers for the Uttar Pradesh class 12 board exam were allegedly leaked on a WhatsApp group.

UP Police Constable recruitment exam cancelled days after paper leakThe Uttar Pradesh Police Constable recruitment exam held on February 17 and 18 was canceled due to a paper leak. The Chief Minister has announced a re-examination within the next six months.

Bihar University: Lessons of the pastPoliticians in Bihar have long been notorious for meddling with higher education. Rules have been changed and appointments made under their pressure - all under the ruse of "creating a better academic climate".
